title: Bhuvneshwar Says He Never Chased a Comeback After Four Years Out
excerpt: Back in India's T20I side for the first time since November 2022, 36-year-old Bhuvneshwar Kumar credited two strong IPL seasons, said he will play the Vijay Hazare and Syed Mushtaq Ali trophies, and insisted a bowler can still control a T20 game.
body:
• Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 36, has returned to India's T20I team after nearly four years, having last played for India in November 2022.
  • He said he did not chase the comeback, crediting his performances in the last two IPL seasons for the recall.
  • Asked about an ODI return with the World Cup less than a year away, he said he is not thinking that far ahead.
  • He confirmed he will play domestic cricket — the Vijay Hazare Trophy and the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy — in the months ahead.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar is proud of his India comeback. He is also clear, in his own telling, that he never organised his career around it.

The 36-year-old seamer returned to the international setup after nearly four years — his last game for India was in November 2022 — earning a recall for the fifth T20I against the West Indies and the ongoing series against New Zealand. Speaking at the press conference in Wellington on Tuesday after India's win in the third T20I, he described what the return felt like, according to IANS.

"To tell you the truth, I did not chase it. Yes, it is a dream. I am very happy to play for India. It is a matter of pride. So I did not know what happened in these four years. Whatever was coming in front of me, the tournaments, the challenges, whatever about cricket, about fitness, I kept doing it."

— Bhuvneshwar Kumar, India fast bowler

Credit to the IPL

Bhuvneshwar said all the credit goes to his last two years in the IPL, where his performances for Royal Challengers Bengaluru paved the way back, according to Sportskeeda's report of the press conference. He has now represented India in 91 T20Is, taking 91 wickets at an average of 24.37 and an economy rate of 7.14, with two five-wicket hauls.

"It feels good to represent India. I wasn't there for many years," he said. "I am feeling good that I've got the opportunity to play for India again."

Domestic cricket next, no long-range plans

Asked about a possible ODI comeback with the ODI World Cup less than a year away, Bhuvneshwar declined to look ahead. "I am not thinking too far ahead, like I did in the last few years. I am happy with what I am getting. Of course, I will play domestic cricket, whether it is Vijay Hazare Trophy or Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. So I am looking forward to that," he said. He last played the 50-over Vijay Hazare Trophy in December 2023, his last List A match nearly three years ago, though he was in action in the SMAT last season.

A bowler's defence

He also pushed back on the idea that T20 cricket now belongs entirely to batters, noting that batting mindsets have changed — batters keep attacking through an innings rather than playing out an over — but insisting the bowler still feeds the ball and can control where it goes. For a seamer whose comeback was built on control rather than pace, it was a fitting summary of how he got back: keep doing the work in front of him, and let the recall take care of itself.
